Include something only when its subject is dsh-kit's own code, configuration or process; when it is about a dependency, leave it out however well-evidenced it looks — including any commit SHA or identifier that belongs to that dependency's repository rather than this one.",

  "last_updated_at": "2026-11-11T16:16:05.115835+00:00",
  "body": "## What the initiative is and why it exists

"Role identity and task lifecycle repair" is dsh-kit's repair programme, launched 2026-11-11, for two coupled defects in `@cc/dsh-taskboard` (ledger, tools, panel, roster) and `@cc/dsh-orchestrator` (root policy, specialist policy, `delegate_task`): (a) a role's identity did not survive the chat that created it, and (b) a task's lifecycle status could disagree with reality. Goals: make role identity explicit and stable, migrate the existing board without history loss, reconcile failed children, and restrict role context where practical. Goal: "A task lifecycle that cannot lie."

Root cause measured in commit 900e7fe (2026-10-30, orchestrator 0.1.8 → 0.1.9, taskboard 0.1.27 → 0.1.28) against `~/tasks/autolabel_pipeline`: 10 roles, 33 tasks, 344 child sessions. The subagent runtime only delivers to a DIRECT child (`dsh-subagent/lib/index.js:1378`), so reuse calls from later chats threw, the orchestrator's bare `catch {}` spawned a new child, and `registerAgent` overwrote the sessionId without a trace.

Symptoms (2026-10-30): the model invented AUDIT, DESIGN, BRIDGE and CORRECTIONS roles while BACKEND, CONFIG and SEGMENTATION existed; delegated work landed as a second row beside the root's task (five such pairs in one chat).

Second measurement, commit a8f4f36 (`~/tasks/3d`): twelve tasks, ten roles; panel read "10 subagents - 1 active 9 sleeping" while every session was four days dead; the `active` row's `lastTaskId` pointed at a removed task; one task sat `ready` with a role and no child; seven of twelve tasks parked in `review` for four days.

Motivating findings on the live `autolabel_pipeline` board (2026-11-11): duplicate role labels carrying different presets; arbitrary custom labels borrowing backend tools (roles not validated as domain entities — an arbitrary CONFIG running on the backend preset); AUDIT used with two presets (reviewer and critic), risking reuse of the wrong specialist; legacy preset-less roles (BRIDGE/CORRECTIONS/DASHBOARD/FPS) still offered in the catalog; an active task whose child failed (a RESEARCH task stayed active although its child ended with `stopReason:error`); and host-wide MCP servers (Godot, Playwright) bloating context for all roles. These findings motivated the initiative.

## The original role model being repaired (2026-10-22 baseline)

Roles were an MVP artifact: `delegate_task` used `role: task.title` and there was no persistent specialist registry. Roles are meant to be persistent, with tasks routed to matching specialists.

Replacement shipped 2026-10-22 as taskboard 0.1.17 / orchestrator 0.1.7 (commit 39a5407, previous integration 472965e8, detail in reports/harness-integration/persistent-roles-handoff.pdf; `make verify` 17/17, kit-update no drift): `delegate_task` requires a persistent role plus optional `roleDescription`; a workspace-level `agents[]` registry of `{ role, label, sessionId, status, taskCount, lastTaskId }`; the first task for a role starts one persistent specialist with a role brief; later tasks reuse the child via `sendMessage`; one child can link many tasks and `childEnded` settles every linked task to review; pause/resume/close/remove restored and agents covered in the roster. The live 3080 process needed a `dsh web` restart and hard refresh.

Persistence boundary: the role record in `.dsh/taskboard.json` survives a DSH restart, but the child session is parent-bound. Within one core root, 40 tasks reuse one child; a new root re-binds the role to a fresh child. True cross-root reuse would need a resident orchestrator session or re-parenting adapter, which DSH ancestry does not allow. Proof: Alpha2 and Beta2 with role BACKEND both linked to `cc7d7b01-…`, both settled to review, registry showed 'BACKEND · sleeping · taskCount 2'.

## P0 — identity: the root policy carries the workspace's roles

P0 (2026-10-30): the root policy carries the workspace's roles read from the ledger at assembly time, so a new chat knows BACKEND exists instead of inventing a synonym.

Same commit: the ledger keeps a `history[]` of superseded session ids with the owning chat, a `generation` counter and `chatSessionId`; the tool result reports `roleRecreated` with the runtime's reason instead of claiming a reuse. A re-created specialist's brief carries the role's last three results and says the code must be re-read: "a summary is a claim about the past, not a reading of the present."

`delegate_task` refuses a new role whose normalized name equals or contains an existing one (BACKEND vs backend vs BACKEND-SAM), listing the names; `forceRole: true` only for a genuinely new domain. The refusal happens before a task is created.

Role identity contract (2026-11-11, `plugins/orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs` + `plugins/taskboard/taskboard.mjs`): a role in the taskboard is a stable (name, preset) pair — one label cannot silently change its tool set. AUDIT is no longer accepted; use REVIEWER with preset reviewer or CRITIC with preset critic. Delegating an existing role with a different preset returns `preset_conflict`, overridable only with explicit `forceRole`. Legacy preset-less roles are marked legacy, shown in a "history only — do not reuse" block, and not reused without an explicit preset. The orchestrator catalog deduplicates roles by (name, preset) and warns about ambiguous names.

Role migration applied to the live `autolabel_pipeline` board (2026-11-11): tasks 225→225, done 211→211, cancelled 5→5, agents 13→12, revision 1936→1937; backup `.dsh/backups/taskboard-2026-11-11T13-28-41-725Z-r1936.json`; a second run returned `changed:false` (idempotent). Current roles: BACKEND[backend], DESIGN[ux], RESEARCH[research], CRITIC[critic], REVIEWER[reviewer], CONCURRENCY[backend], CONFIG[backend], SEGMENTATION[backend], UX/UI[ux]; legacy: BRIDGE, CORRECTIONS, DASHBOARD, FPS.

## P1 — "one piece of work, one row"

P1 (2026-10-30): `delegate_task(taskId)` attaches to an existing task — which must be open, not paused, and owned by this role or none — instead of creating a second one; `update()` can set a task's role, which is how the attach names the specialty. This targets the observed duplicate rows.

## P2 — not built by agreement

Explicitly not done (2026-10-30): the specialist session still belongs to the chat that created it. P2 — specialists as root-kind sessions dispatched through the session controller — is scoped but not built. Role identity across chats remains repaired only in the P0 sense (the role and its record survive; the child is recreated and the recreation is reported).

## Board honesty: orphan/stale annotation and cleanup

Role rows are annotated on READ, never rewritten by a read (2026-11-02): `orphan` when the claimed task is gone, `stale` when untouched for a day (config `staleAfterMs`). The panel counts `active` only from rows that are neither, shows `N stale` in the header, and renders the chip with the reason in its title.

`remove()` now clears agent rows by `lastTaskId` as well; the old `childSessionIds`-only cleanup missed a delegation that registered its role but never linked the task (2026-11-02).

The root policy appends a board-debt block (2026-11-02): `review` tasks with the age of the oldest, and `ready` tasks with a role but no child, naming the ids to attach with `delegate_task(taskId: ...)`. `active` with no child is NOT debt — that is allowed inline work.

## T1–T4 programme of 2026-11-10

Status (2026-11-10, REF-ID: conversation:session-84256a92-009f-4683-99fe-6674bfe317d5): T1 (taskboard per chat) done, proven, committed as f80d7b8; T2 (six role presets) code written, YAML validated, plugins rebuilt and installed but unverified on a live harness; T3 (Excalidraw map) decision recorded; T4 (plugin audit) not started.

Planned order: T2 — six presets (orchestrator + UX/UI, BACKEND, RESEARCH, REVIEWER, DOCS) with personas, tool sets and `delegate_task` role choice → T3 the map → T4 plugin audit (separate child). T1 sat in review on that chat's board.

Per-chat board (T1, taskboard 0.1.33 / orchestrator 0.1.18, 2026-11-10): `chatId` is the root session of the creating lineage, so a delegated child's task lands on the parent chat's board; reads default to the caller's chat, with `task_list` scope `workspace` and the panel's All chats toggle reading the whole history with foreign rows marked; pre-`chatId` rows fall back to `parentSessionId`; agent writes from another chat are refused with `other_chat`; `delegate_task` refuses to attach to another chat's task before starting a child. One `.dsh/taskboard.json` per workspace with a chat column, not a file per chat. Rationale: "A fresh chat opened onto every other chat's work and the agent could not tell which rows were its own; one file with a chat column keeps history from drifting from the ledger."

## T9 — the task lifecycle that cannot lie (accepted 2026-11-10)

T9 accepted 2026-11-10 on taskboard 0.1.37, orchestrator 0.1.22, babysitter 0.1.6; evidence is `/tmp/lifecycle-host-proof.mjs` (exit 0), with every illegal transition rejected by its own code: `needs_role_or_inline`, `needs_result`, `needs_evidence`, `needs_reason`, `needs_review`, `use_close/pause/resume`, `terminal`, `other_chat`; legacy `proposed/ready` display as `open` without rewriting the file; `make verify` 17/17 plus docs.

Boundaries kept: `task_close` only from `review` (abandoned work is `cancelled`), and `childEnded` moves `active→review` without a result because it is a runtime event. Refined 2026-11-11: if a child ends with error, aborted, interrupted, cancelled, timeout or failed, the task goes to `blocked`, not `review`. A `reconcile` pass moves stuck `active` tasks to `blocked`/`review`, but only when all linked children have already ended — a running child is never touched.

Invariants as adversarially tested: `open → active` requires role + owner (delegation) or explicit inline; `active → review` requires `result.summary` and evidence; `review → done` only through acceptance; `blocked` requires a reason; `cancelled` is terminal and unreachable from done; every task has a role (and preset) or `inline: true`. Nothing legal was refused.

Structural change: statuses collapse to open/active/paused/review/done/blocked/cancelled (legacy display-mapped on read, files never rewritten); `transitionRefusal()` is the single host enforcement point with named codes; the list shows Status/Role/Task/Owner/Updated, the board has 5 columns, the roster counts only this chat's roles.

Standing convention restated 2026-11-11: any work changing code, config, docs, migration or a test artifact starts as a task — `task_create` with objective, scope, nonScope, acceptance; `task_update` to active before starting; `task_note` for intermediate state; `task_update` to review only with `resultSummary` and evidence; `task_close` only after human acceptance. No active task may be left if its child errored or already returned a result.

## Taskboard 0.1.39 / 0.1.41 — cancel, assignment, compare-and-set

0.1.41 (2026-11-11): real `task_cancel` (paused and child-bearing tasks could never be cancelled); assignment path (`task_update` + panel accept role/inline/owner, so the 97 pre-role rows can reach active); tasks born `open` via `initial_status`; a blocked task cannot lose its reason; compare-and-set (`needs_revision`) for every command-path mutation; `needs_result` on `task_close`; the header badge resolving the chat like the pane; split limits (`maxTasks` for work in flight, `maxRows` / `board_rows_full` as a separate file guard).

## Role = preset: the 2026-11-10/11 contract

Roles become tool sets (taskboard 0.1.33 / orchestrator 0.1.18, 2026-11-10): agent presets in the profile patch — orchestrator (default system designer: read/readImage, grep/glob, web, goals, taskboard, delegation, no bash/write/edit), ux, backend, research (no shell, no surgical edit), reviewer (run and read, not write), docs (full shell and fs); standard stays as the hands-on escape hatch. `delegate_task` maps role to preset and passes `agentPreset`; a provider without `capabilities.agentPreset` is refused before a child exists. A role's session is reused only when its recorded preset matches. Kit tools register per agent on `agent/created` and `agent.ctx.tools.register`: `papers_*` research only, `babysitter_*` orchestrator only, diagram/presentation orchestrator + ux; a session with no recorded preset keeps them. Rationale: "A role written in a brief is a request; a role that decides which tools exist is a contract."

The roster grew from six presets to seven with `critic` (adversarial general tester: bash+fs+web, no browser, break-within-constraints, never fix); "six roles" revised to "seven". Orchestrator 0.1.23 maps CRITIC / CRITIC-GENERAL / TESTER / QA -> critic, while AUDIT stays reviewer. Measured live: a critic child found two real contract violations in a disposable Node library.

Canonical roles adopted 2026-11-11: UX/UI→ux, BACKEND→backend, RESEARCH→research, REVIEWER→reviewer, CRITIC→critic, DOCS→docs; every `delegate_task` passes explicit role and preset, with no implicit preset inference from the name. Basis: agent presets (preset = persona + plugin list, each child its own composition) plus `dsh-tool-subagent` with `agentPreset` / `allowedAgentPresets` — tool isolation is structural, not prompt-based. One task, one child: re-delegation passes `taskId` so no duplicate row is created, and each child has one task and one preset.

Legacy preset-less roles BRIDGE, CORRECTIONS, DASHBOARD and FPS must not be used (2026-11-11): their sessions lack a role persona and normal toolset (only generic policy and `run_code`). Removed from the workflow; historical tasks not rewritten, but no new tasks on them.

Orchestrator contract (2026-11-11): a role is a stable (name, preset) pair, not just a label — one label cannot silently change its tool set; the child's real context is the agent preset (backend gets bash/edit/write, ux the UX tools, research no bash/edit, reviewer/critic no edit/write, docs writes documentation), so the role is chosen by the tools needed, not by the task's name. New roles must not be invented ad hoc. The orchestrator does not write code: it reads, designs, creates tasks, delegates, verifies evidence and integrates; final integration is never delegated. Before delegating it checks the role catalog and board debt: no dormant role with mismatched preset, no BACKEND-2/BACKEND-NEW when BACKEND can be reused, no new role until its preset's difference is clear.

Babysitter tasks are created without a role, so they don't pollute the `agents[]` roster; `delegate_task` can accept such a task (role matches or is absent) but won't assign it a role. `parentSessionId` is not set (unlike `delegate_task` tasks) — cosmetic only.

## Root-only role guard (2026-11-11)

Root-only `tools.guard` added in `plugins/orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs` (2026-11-11): forbids the root agent from calling `subagent`/`subagent_fork` and directs it to `delegate_task(role=...)`; specialists keep their own subagent tools. Motive: an audit found 3 subagents (a89c91e0, 92a56489, 63ee9c52) running with full root tools because direct subagent calls bypassed `delegate_task`; `task_link` only records a role label, not preset/persona/tools. Shipped in `@cc/dsh-orchestrator` 0.1.26 (2026-11-11).

Deployment consequence: the `subagent` tool is disabled for the root agent — calling it directly returns a refusal and no child is created. Root delegation must go through `delegate_task` with a role (BACKEND, UX/UI, RESEARCH, REVIEWER, CRITIC, DOCS, or a catalog role) so the child gets its preset, persona, restricted tools and task link — or the work is inline. The gate is a deployment policy, not a malformed argument. `rules/DEPLOYMENT.md` documents that the four spawn paths share the one subagent service and that root delegation is intended to go through `delegate_task`.

Orchestrator 0.1.24 (2026-11-11): `delegate_task` stops at the first taskboard refusal (no child on `board_full`, stale or `other_chat`; the row is blocked with the code), a refused `linkChild` interrupts the child it could not record, and root detection follows `parentSession`/`origin` instead of depth alone.

## Prompt-cost and state-truthfulness follow-ups

orchestrator 0.1.15 (2026-11-09, shipped 2026-11-11) made the role catalog and board debt render once per turn via a `freezePerTurn(render)` helper in `plugins/orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs` (lines 181-215), memo reset by a `session/event` → `turn/start` subscription (lines 583-616), so the system prompt stays byte-stable for all steps of a turn; children unaffected because CHILD_POLICY is static. In the quota-breaking kimi session, 19 of 20 rewritten-prompt steps returned cacheRead=1792 while context was 200–310K tokens: 4.2M of that session's 5.0M fresh input. Prompt-cache thrashing from per-turn rewrites was the main driver of the quota blowout.

Live running state (2026-11-11): dsh-kit added live task-running-state display to the taskboard and a hooks bridge, plus an image-window request plugin; deployment/help docs updated, artifacts repacked. In `@cc/dsh-taskboard` 0.1.45 an active child shows as `active` when the live session is actually running, instead of a stale `sleeping`.

Known limitation still open (2026-11-11): host-wide tools (MCP/Hindsight/taskboard) remain visible to all roles; presets restrict only a role's own tools. Per-role separation needs a separate MCP server per role — a distinct architectural decision described in the child policy and docs, unresolved as of 2026-11-11. The preset panel in that workspace shows historical taskboard labels, not plugin lists: `orchestrator.mjs` (lines ~78-128) defines only ux, backend, research, reviewer, critic, docs (plus orchestrator), with ROLE_PRESETS mapping audit→reviewer by default; all current child agents run on deepseek-official/deepseek-flash with reasoningEffort: high.

Test-cases panel UX repair (2026-11-11, @cc/dsh-test-cases 0.1.9, part of commit `f0781c1`), fixing four owner-reported bugs: (1) every row and the detail view now show a `STATUS` with a text status and explanation (`Verified — a run or observation is recorded.`); (2) new host tool `case_remove` — only for `deprecated`/`superseded` cases, compare-and-set on revision, mandatory confirmation in the UI, audit line in `docs/cases/.removed.jsonl`, active cases refused with `CASE_NOT_REMOVABLE`; (3) `Hide detail`/`Show detail` buttons, the list widening from 390 to 1160 px while keeping filters and the selected case; (4) long detail scrolls inside the panel without moving the page, verified at 1440 and 760 px.

## Design map v2 — visual vocabulary, preview and health (2026-11-11)

The design-map plugin (`plugins/design-map`) was reworked on 2026-11-11: `layout.js`, `preview.js` and `index.js` were rewritten, `index.js` being the core change, with `preview.js` added as a new file. Goal: make the map easier for the agent to use — so it explicitly understands the visual representation it is producing — and as easy as possible for the user to read and edit.

Diagnosis at rev 28 of `design.excalidraw` (2026-11-11): six of eight blocks had a two-line label in a 24px text element inside a 76px block, spilling past the frame; blocks `web` and neighbour `oweb` overlapped; `roles` sat at (0,0). Root cause of "the agent does not understand what it is drawing": `edge.label` and `title` were stored in customData/meta and returned by `read`, but never drawn — no text on arrows, no map title. `read` always answered `ok: true` with no geometry checks, so the agent never learned the map was broken, and the only repair (`layout`) was invisible until write.

Visual vocabulary: `kind` → shape (`service` rectangle, `store` ellipse, `decision` diamond, `external` dashed); `layer` puts a node into a titled band (no layers → the previous plain graph); `title` and `edges[].label` are now really drawn — the title as a text element on top, the edge label as bound text on the arrow, editable by double click.

Accepted decision (2026-11-11): add `preview` — a deterministic, token-cheap text render of the real geometry (columns → blocks → arrows → labels) — and `health` — the same `analyzeElements` checks already run before write. Implemented: every design-map tool response now carries `preview` (columns = actual x-ranges, rows = actual layers) and `health` (list of problems: clip, overlap, edge_cross, etc.) via the new `preview.js`.

Layer grouping was measured in a real frame and rejected: a group dragged the whole layer when one block was moved, breaking per-node dragging and editing. Instead the layer band is a locked decoration (not a group) and all labels are real bound texts (2026-11-11).

An independent REVIEWER found six defects, all fixed and closed with regressions K1–K6 (2026-11-11): bindings of ellipse/diamond on `remove` and in health; duplicated label of a human-edited arrow; deadlock when deleting a band (`layer_id` + self-healing); two "truths" for the title (now only the drawn element); `layers[]` order (reordered by `layout`, not by upsert). Two defects shared one root — shapes were treated as rectangles.

Verification: `node --check` on `layout.js`; generator `gen-v2.mjs` with scenes 'plain' and 'layers'; `ops.mjs` operation test; `reports/design-map-layout/validator-cases.mjs`; Playwright harness renders on 127.0.0.1:8791 and 127.0.0.1:8792. `node reports/design-map-v2/cases.mjs` → 76 PASS, 0 FAIL, exit 0; old validator cases all passed; `make verify` 17/17 + documentation ok; tarball 0.2.0 (sha256 `5d40a47f…547a58`) matches source; harness render matched `03-layered-map.png` byte-for-byte. Evidence package under `reports/design-map-v2/` (cases.mjs, gen-fixtures.mjs, fixtures/, harness/, EVIDENCE.md) with screenshots 01-before-live-map.png, 02-after-layout.png, 03-layered-map.png, 04-shapes-and-labels.png.

Documented and repacked 2026-11-11 as version 0.2.0: README written at `plugins/design-map/README.md`, root README/USERGUIDE and `profile/cordis.patch.yml` updated, plugin rebuilt to `plugins/cc-dsh-design-map-0.2.0.tgz` via `scripts/pack-plugin.mjs` (old 0.1.21 tgz removed). Shipped in commit `f2b4876` "Give the design map a visual vocabulary and an agent preview" (10 files, +1205/−280), pushed `f0781c1..f2b4876` to origin/main (exit 0, local == remote, tree clean); the push also accepted three tasks in review (task-mwc8jac0-zzro1j, task-mwc9cdt0-4rshi5, task-mwc9c1bx-8tcoob), which were closed.

Known limitations (2026-11-11): arrows may cross each other (the validator catches only an arrow passing through a block, not arrow-arrow crossings); rotated labels may shift slightly; performance above 18 nodes is unmeasured; in 0.2.0 labels of two arrows at one block may crowd; upsert does not reorder existing bands — that needs `layout`. UI decision: the panel does not grow "fix it" buttons — the human reports a bad map in chat, and editing stays live; the full vocabulary (shapes + layer containers) is adopted.

## Current state, as recorded

Done and proven: T1 per-chat taskboard (f80d7b8); persistent roles with `agents[]` (2026-10-22, 39a5407); P0 role identity plus `history[]`/`generation`/`chatSessionId`/`roleRecreated` (900e7fe, 2026-10-30); P1 `delegate_task(taskId)` attach (2026-10-30); orphan/stale read-time annotation, `lastTaskId` cleanup and the board-debt block (2026-11-02, a8f4f36); T9 host-enforced lifecycle with named refusal codes (taskboard 0.1.37, accepted 2026-11-10); taskboard 0.1.39 and 0.1.41 (cancel, assignment, compare-and-set, split limits, 2026-11-11); seven role presets including `critic` (2026-11-10); canonical role→preset contract and legacy-role retirement (2026-11-11); root-only `tools.guard` in orchestrator 0.1.26 and `delegate_task` stopping at the first refusal in 0.1.24 (2026-11-11); live running state in taskboard 0.1.45 (2026-11-11); stable (name, preset) role-identity contract with `preset_conflict`/`forceRole`, legacy "history only" marking and catalog dedup, plus failed-child → `blocked` and `reconcile` (2026-11-11); role migration applied idempotently to the live board (2026-11-11); design-map 0.2.0 with visual vocabulary, `preview`/`health` and K1–K6 regressions (2026-11-11). Committed and pushed 2026-11-11 as `f0781c1` "Fix role identity contract and test-cases panel UX", then `f2b4876` "Give the design map a visual vocabulary and an agent preview" (push `f0781c1..f2b4876 main -> main`, HEAD = origin/main, working tree clean). Gates: `make verify` exit 0 (17/17 packaging/portability, documentation ok), `scripts/taskboard-role-proof.mjs` 15/15 (4/15, exit 1 against the pre-fix modules), `case-library.test.mjs` 4 pass, `git diff --check` exit 0, usability-proof 15/15 PASS, design-map `cases.mjs` 76 PASS / 0 FAIL. New versions: @cc/dsh-orchestrator 0.1.31, @cc/dsh-taskboard 0.1.48, @cc/dsh-test-cases 0.1.9, @cc/dsh-design-map 0.2.0.

Not built: P2 — specialists as root-kind sessions dispatched through the session controller — so a specialist session still belongs to the chat that created it (2026-10-30, no later record of it being built).

Still open (2026-11-11): role enforcement is not registration-level (roles are labels, presets are the contract, an arbitrary label can still run on a preset unless refused); host-wide MCP context bloat for every role — a critic child still receives 26 `mcp__playwright__*` tools despite its preset (tracked as T7, unresolved), and per-role separation needs a separate MCP server per role; the live :3080 process still runs older versions (orchestrator 0.1.26, taskboard 0.1.45, test-cases 0.1.7) and needs a Harness restart; `kit-update --check` reports actions=install-plugins,write-rules; the migrated tasks sit in `review` awaiting owner acceptance.

Worked as a tracked task (2026-11-11): on the request "Исправь найденные проблемы" the agent created `task-mwc5e85w-e52p1d` with goal and initiative, delegated the role-contract and test-cases-panel fixes, recorded the owner's requirements via `case_record`, and ran `scripts/taskboard-role-proof.mjs` and `make verify` as proof.
"
}
